texts: Diastole is more energy dependent than systole: B is the answer.
Relaxation needs energy to pump calcium back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum and to release the actin and myosin cross-bridges.
That is why, when coronary flow runs short, relaxation fails before contraction does.
The main fuel of the heart is fatty acids, not glucose, and a thicker wall lowers wall stress rather than raising it.
Memory hook: the biggest pile of coal goes in when the fan is pulled open to rest, and the furnace runs on oil barrels, not sugar.
